subject: DPA Annex: On-Prem / VPC Egress & Operational Evidence
messages:
From: Samantha Reed <privacy@novushealth.com>

Cc: Tom Alvarez <legal@novushealth.com>, procurement@novushealth.com
Date: Tue, 4 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA Annex follow-up — on-prem / VPC egress questions

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we continue our legal review, our Data Protection Officer flagged a couple of detailed questions for the DPA Annex related to on-prem and VPC-hosted deployments:

1) For customers choosing Private (VPC) or On‑Prem deployments, can you describe the egress controls and data path? Specifically: which Redwood components (control plane, logging, telemetry) communicate outside the customer VPC, to which endpoints, and what data is sent?

2) We need evidence of technical safeguards (network diagrams, firewall rules, IP ranges, and a sample audit log) that demonstrate no customer PII leaves their VPC unless explicitly configured.

3) If a customer requests a fully air‑gapped on‑prem install, what exactly is included in the deliverable and what operational steps are required from Novus IT?

Please send the DPA Annex response and any attachments you can share for procurement/legal review. If you need, we can schedule a short follow-up call.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we are aiming to close procurement by end of month.

Best,
Samantha Reed
Privacy & Compliance Lead
Novus Health

Attachments: none
From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Reed <privacy@novushealth.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <legal@novushealth.com>, procurement@novushealth.com
Date: Tue, 4 Mar 2025 12:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA Annex follow-up — on-prem / VPC egress questions

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; attaching a DPA Annex draft and a VPC egress flowchart for your legal/IT team.

1) Control plane: the Redwood control plane (control.redwood.ai) communicates with management endpoints for billing, license checks, and updates. For Private (VPC) customers the control plane only sends metadata (instance health checks, anonymized telemetry if enabled) over TLS to our control endpoints.

2) Data path and egress: customer request payloads and model artifacts remain within the customer VPC or on‑prem runtime. By default, inference traffic and token payloads do not traverse Redwood-hosted networks when using Private or On‑Prem modes. Telemetry is opt‑in and can be disabled. We detail firewall/IP ranges in the flowchart.

3) Air‑gapped on‑prem: we provide an installer bundle (runtime binaries, inference engine, model weights) and an operational runbook. The bundle includes a local-only control stub; optional automation integration points (e.g., local monitoring exporters) are documented but not required. The customer must provide host networking, KMS/HSM integration if desired, and an internal package distribution mechanism.

I’ve attached: 1) Redwood_DPA_Annex_Response.pdf (redacted example evidence), 2) VPC_Egress_Flowchart.png. Follow-ups: we can provide a sanitized sample audit log showing request URIs (no customer PII) under NDA.

Would you like a call Thursday to walk the Novus IT team through the flowchart?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- 2025-03-05_Redwood_DPA_Annex_Response.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 5 Mar 2025 08:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: DPA Annex follow-up — on-prem / VPC egress questions

Jordan — quick answers below and attaching the telemetry field list.

Telemetry (Private / VPC default):
- heartbeat_ping: instance id, timestamp, status_code (retained 30 days)
- runtime_metrics: cpu_percent, gpu_utilization, memory_bytes (retained 14 days)
- anonymized_error_counts: error_code, count (retained 90 days)

We do NOT capture request payloads or generated tokens as telemetry in Private or On‑Prem modes. Customers can opt‑out via the console or the private config file (private_config.telemetry.enabled = false).

Attached: 2025-03-05_Redwood_Telemetry_Fields.csv

Ben — sample audit log?

—Marissa

Jordan / Marissa — attached is a sanitized one-hour audit excerpt (UTC timestamps, masked ids). Fields included: request_id, instance_id, endpoint, status_code, bytes_in, bytes_out, auth_method, action (inference/healthcheck). Retention: audit logs stored for configurable period; default 180 days for Dedicated/Private.

I’ve also included notes on how to configure local log retention in on‑prem installs (logrotate + retention config in /etc/redwood/logging.conf).

Tom — quick confirmations and next steps: 

1) Integrity: yes — for air‑gapped bundles we provide a signed SHA256 manifest and GPG-signed release notes. We include verification instructions in the runbook (verify-sha256.sh + gpg --verify examples).

2) Support: we offer an offline support plan that includes a dedicated technical lead reachable via customer VPN (mutual TLS) or scheduled encrypted swap media. Remote troubleshooting for air‑gapped installs is provided over customer-controlled channels; escalation to code-level fixes is available under a paid SLA (details attached).

Attached: 2025-03-07_Redwood_Onprem_Deployment_Runbook.docx (Runbook with integrity and support steps)
